resources.string: Draws the sound of about 20 seconds of this song so you can see whether it is real lossless quality. Playback is not affected.
Sound reaches up to %1$.1f kHz. The top of the chart is %2$.1f kHz.
Couldn\'t tell where the sound stops. The top of the chart is %1$.1f kHz.
Can\'t tell from this part of the song
Probably upscaled from a lower-quality copy
Up = higher pitch: bass at the bottom, cymbals at the top. The top is half the sample rate, the highest pitch the file can hold (22 kHz for 44.1 kHz audio). Left to right = time.
Colour = how loud that pitch is, from black (silent) through purple, red and yellow to white (loudest).
Real lossless music usually has sound almost to the top. If everything above one sharp line is dark, the file was probably made from an MP3 or AAC copy; those usually stop around 16–20 kHz.
